lab.title: knn.py — bench
lab.prompt: k-NN has no training step. To predict, you measure the distance from the new point to every stored point, take the k closest, and let them vote. Implement euclidean(a, b) — the straight-line distance between two equal-length lists of numbers — and knn_predict(points, labels, query, k) — the majority label among the k nearest points.

lab.solution:
import math
from collections import Counter


def euclidean(a, b):
    return math.sqrt(sum((x - y) ** 2 for x, y in zip(a, b)))


def knn_predict(points, labels, query, k):
    ranked = sorted(zip(points, labels), key=lambda pl: euclidean(pl[0], query))
    top = [label for _, label in ranked[:k]]
    return Counter(top).most_common(1)[0][0]


pts = [[0, 0], [1, 1], [0, 1], [8, 8], [9, 9], [8, 9]]
lbls = ["A", "A", "A", "B", "B", "B"]
print(knn_predict(pts, lbls, [1, 0], 3))
